structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single candidate Pre-Python architecture/design document for providers, routing, and cost/token budgets, limited to documentation and local packet/readiness evidence, using existing cited authority rather than inventing adopted architecture or implementation behavior.
structuredContent.summary: The work packet has a clear bounded outcome: produce docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/providers-and-budgets.md as a reviewable CANDIDATE design artifact covering provider capability/version evidence, cheapest-capable/local-first routing, and hard BIU/project/deployment/retry budget governance. It explicitly excludes implementation, source/test/config changes, paid calls, secrets, public publication, EOS edits, and Founder approval. The cited authority and acceptance criteria are sufficient to draft the candidate document and record any unresolved Founder decisions instead of deciding them silently.
implementation_unknowns: Locate and map the named local source baselines and prior decisions to concrete source/invariant sections without adopting uncited neighboring documents implicitly.
Determine the existing documentation packet/readiness evidence conventions and exact local paths under docs/work-units/pre-python-gate for any permitted receipts.

Extract the relevant provider adapter behavior, dispatcher/runtime reservation behavior, subscription/list-cost observations, and historical decisions accurately enough to cite them as evidence without claiming fresh runtime verification.
Formulate successful and failing examples that are faithful to the cited authority while clearly labeling proposed architecture/security/storage semantics as CANDIDATE.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through document review: the artifact either exists at the required path, is labeled candidate, changes only allowed documentation/evidence locations, maps source authority to invariants, covers G17/G18/G24, separates list/subscription observations from monetary charges, authorizes no paid calls, includes successful and failing examples, records unresolved Founder decisions, and avoids implementation claims. One independent content review against the provided rows and cited authority is meaningful because the deliverable is a single cohesive design document rather than multiple independently adoptable architecture decisions.
material_risks: The document could overstep by converting candidate design into adopted architecture or implementation authorization.
The author could accidentally invent provider ranking, model hierarchy, billing semantics, or compatibility rules not supported by the cited authority.
The author could blur subscription/list-cost observations with actual monetary charges or imply paid execution authority.
Cross-document dependencies may tempt implicit adoption of neighboring candidate material rather than recording unresolved choices.
Historical Node evidence may be overstated as fresh regression proof or Python capability proof.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the candidate design document and permitted local packet/readiness evidence, then perform an independent content review against G17, G18, G24, the binding authority, and the stated exclusions.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the owner intent, scope, authority, exclusions, and acceptance criteria are explicit. Remaining uncertainty is implementation/documentation research: finding and accurately citing the existing materials, not deciding unresolved product or architecture intent. The three topic areas are tightly coupled by provider capability evidence, routing choice, and cost governance, so splitting would reduce coherence rather than isolate independent decisions. No supplied evidence establishes a missing prerequisite or conflicting repository ownership; the task itself states the necessary source documents exist in named local baselines and that no runtime reruns are warranted for this documentation-only unit.
